clue.text: Mark isn't included

parts.note: read as a description of the punctuation mark that sits inside the word isn't itself, standing in for the missing O

explanation.surface: Someone called Mark has been left out of a group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name left off a list; it is a punctuation mark, the one actually written in the word isn't.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised comma marking the dropped letter in a contraction such as isn't is this punctuation sign.

clue.text: Losing head, is angry for a long time

indicators.note: losing its head means the word for being angry drops its opening letter

parts.note: someone who is angry rages

explanation.surface: A person who loses their temper stays furious for a long while.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatic: waiting ages means waiting for a long time, used adverbially.

clue.text: Living things in grass? Mom almost in a frenzy

indicators.note: in a frenzy suggests wild disorder, so the gathered letters are thrown about

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: almost means the word Mom loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A mother panics over the creatures living in the lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims Mom to MO; 'in a frenzy' then rearranges IN, GRASS and MO together.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: organisms are individual living beings such as plants, animals or microbes.

clue.text: Mad Hatter not hard to deal with

indicators.note: mad suggests deranged, so the remaining letters are jumbled
not hard means the letter H, the pencil abbreviation for hard, is removed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The Mad Hatter of Alice in Wonderland is an easy fellow to handle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not hard' removes H (hard, as on pencils) from HATTER, leaving ATTER, which 'Mad' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to treat a matter or person is to deal with them.

clue.text: Bachelor going after love? Wait and see

indicators.note: going after places the bachelor's letter behind the letter for love

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
to wait at table is to serve

explanation.surface: A single man chasing romance is told to bide his time and see what happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wait and see' reads as one phrase; 'Wait' gives SERVE and 'see' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to observe something is to see or notice it.

clue.text: Worker was first to be manipulated

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
someone who was first in a race led

explanation.surface: A labourer who came first was then used by others.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something handled has been physically worked or manipulated with the hands.

clue.text: Nick Nolte's first to get in drink

indicators.note: to get in places the chosen letter inside the word for a drink

parts.note: to sip is to drink in small amounts

indicators.note: first signals the opening letter of the actor's name

explanation.surface: The actor Nick Nolte is first to get a round in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick Nolte' looks like the actor's full name, but Nick is the definition, a small cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a snip is a small cut, just like a nick.

clue.text: French city north of Rouen's beginning to be more pleasant

indicators.note: in a down clue north of puts the city above, before, the next letter

parts.note: Nice is a city on the French Riviera

indicators.note: beginning signals the opening letter of Rouen

explanation.surface: A French city to the north of Rouen is about to become more pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative synonym: nicer means pleasanter, more agreeable.

clue.text: Step outside steamship with awfully green travellers

indicators.note: outside means the dance step goes around the rest

parts.note: pas is a dance step in ballet

indicators.note: awfully suggests something badly done, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Seasick travellers step out of a steamship looking very green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' looks like it qualifies 'green' as seasick; it turns GREEN into ENGER, and the dance step PAS splits to go 'outside' the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: passengers are people travelling in a vehicle or vessel.

clue.text: Wild glee after securing a great score in golf

indicators.note: after securing means the scrambled word wraps around the single letter
wild suggests chaos, so the letters of glee are rearranged

explanation.surface: A golfer whoops with delight after landing a great score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges GLEE into EGLE, which holds A.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf term: an eagle is two strokes under par on a hole, a very good score.

clue.text: Books are full of these judgements

definitions.meaning: books are made up of grammatical units of words, each ending with a full stop
a judge passes punishments on convicted people

explanation.surface: Books are crammed with verdicts.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: grammatical word groups making up prose, and the punishments a court hands down.

clue.text: Consider a short period in river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, south-west England
min is short for minute, a short period

explanation.surface: Think about spending a brief while in the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to examine something is to consider or inspect it closely.

clue.text: Turn somersaults around a boy? That's normal

indicators.note: around means the rearranged word wraps the single letter
somersaults suggests tumbling over, so the word turn is scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
Al is a boy's name, short for Alan or Albert

explanation.surface: A boy turning cartwheels? Perfectly ordinary behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somersaults' rearranges TURN into NTUR, not a simple reversal, before it goes 'around' the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something natural is normal, as expected.

clue.text: Own part of a golf course with no name

indicators.note: with no name means the letter N, abbreviation for name, is dropped

parts.note: a green is a part of a golf course, the putting surface

explanation.surface: Someone owns a piece of a golf course that has no name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Own' looks like possession but is the verb meaning admit or concede.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to own (up) is to admit or concede, which is to agree.

clue.text: Where you might see flowers swing to and fro close to Epping Forest

parts.note: to rock is to swing back and forth

indicators.note: close to signals the closing letter of Epping

parts.note: Arden is a forest in Warwickshire, the setting of As You Like It

explanation.surface: Flowers swaying gently near Epping Forest, an ancient woodland north-east of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Epping Forest' reads as one place; only its first word's last letter, G, is used, and 'Forest' is a different forest, ARDEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a garden built among stones, planted with alpine flowers.

clue.text: Offensive person's smell returned — an uncomfortable situation

indicators.note: returned means the letters for a body smell are read backwards

parts.note: BO is body odour, a person's smell
a scene is an embarrassing public fuss

explanation.surface: Someone's body odour came back, causing an awkward moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something obscene is grossly offensive or indecent.

clue.text: Grave words

parts.note: read not as solemn speech but as words written on a grave, the inscription on a tombstone

explanation.definitionFit: Literally: an inscription carved on a headstone in memory of the dead person.

clue.text: Compelling daughter to call around six

indicators.note: around means the word for phoning wraps the Roman numeral

parts.note: to ring is to call on the telephone
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A daughter phones about six o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a driving force is compelling, urgent and forceful.

clue.text: Hobbies in street worried last of sparrows

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: worried suggests agitation, so these letters are churned around

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: last of signals the final letter of sparrows

explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word placing the hobbies; it is a piece, and 'worried' rearranges STREET into TEREST.

clue.text: Caressing skin is surprisingly good

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests an unexpected outcome, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Stroking someone's skin feels unexpectedly nice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges SKIN and IS into KISSIN, and G is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Near synonym: kissing is a form of caressing or affectionate touching.

clue.text: Rubbish container in French station

indicators.note: in puts the container inside the French word for a station

parts.note: gare is French for railway station
a bag is a container

explanation.surface: Refuse sacks pile up in a Paris railway terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: garbage is rubbish, waste to be thrown away.

clue.text: Larger kitchen equipment by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it means the word is pronounced like the kitchen gadget

parts.note: a grater is a kitchen tool for shredding cheese

explanation.surface: A bigger set of cooking utensils, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: greater means larger in size or amount.

clue.text: Adult woman, new in class

indicators.note: in places the two letters inside the word for a class

parts.note: a class is a group of things or people

explanation.surface: A mature woman joins a fresh class.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a grown-up is an adult.

clue.text: Fragrance obtained from a gypsy

parts.note: Roma is the name of the Romani people, once called gypsies

explanation.surface: A traveller sells perfume.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an aroma is a pleasant smell, a fragrance.

clue.text: Scoundrel beheaded animal

parts.note: a rotter is a cad or scoundrel

explanation.surface: A villain decapitated a creature.

clue.text: List includes old bird

indicators.note: includes means the list word wraps around the letter

parts.note: a roster is a list of names on duty

explanation.surface: The register contains an elderly bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a rooster is a male chicken, a farmyard bird.

clue.text: Race goes almost round Britain

parts.note: goes in the sense of attempts: has a go, tries

explanation.walkthrough: 'goes' means attempts, TRIES; 'almost' cuts it to TRIE, which goes 'round' B.
explanation.definitionFit: Near synonym: a tribe is a people or ethnic group, a race.

clue.text: Refuse collection from garden, yesterday

indicators.note: collection from suggests letters gathered out of the run of the following words

explanation.surface: Garden waste was picked up yesterday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like rubbish; it is the verb, to decline.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to deny someone something is to refuse it.

clue.text: Where farmer can keep things from wife — right inside bar

clue.text: Problem children

definitions.meaning: a matter of concern or difficulty to be resolved
offspring, as in died without legal descendants

clue.text: Average achievement from women or men

indicators.note: from indicates letters taken out of the words that follow

clue.text: In a vulnerable manner, ill sheep slaughtered without one knowing

without one means the Roman numeral I is removed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
